findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?' so it never runs
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializer decides whether to emit an attribute by calling `include_<attribute>?`. This guard is named `include_website_name` (no trailing `?`), so it is never invoked and `website_name` is emitted for every serialized user, including users with no website (as `null`). The intended `website.present?` condition has no effect. Rename it to `include_website_name?`, or (better, see the trust-level finding) move `website_name` into `untrusted_attributes`.

findings.title: website_name leaks a website that untrusted_attributes deliberately hides
findings.body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111) so that a TL0 user's profile fields are not exposed to anonymous visitors (`scope.restrict_user_fields?`). The new `website_name` attribute is added to the plain `attributes` list and has no such guard: its `include_website_name` method only checks `website.present?` and, being misnamed, is not called anyway. As a result anonymous visitors now receive `website_name` containing the hidden TL0 user's website host and path, defeating the anti-spam restriction. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (and make the include check honour `restrict_user_fields?`).

findings.title: Gating the website block on model.website_name hides websites the serializer cannot parse
findings.body: The block that renders the globe icon and the website link is now guarded by `{{#if model.website_name}}`. The serializer returns `nil` whenever `URI(website.to_s)` raises (e.g. a URL containing a space such as `http://example.com/my page`), and it is also absent if an endpoint does not include the new attribute. Previously the display name was derived in JS from `model.website` (`website.split('/')[2]`), so such a user still saw the globe and a link. Now the website silently disappears from the profile even though `model.website` is present. Gate on `model.website` and fall back to a derived name, or make the serializer always return a non-nil name when the website is present.

findings.title: untested: website_name is not added to the untrusted attributes spec
findings.body: The `untrusted_attributes` list still contains only the original attributes. Because `website_name` is not added, there is no test asserting that the new field is omitted for a TL0 user seen as anonymous, so the leak of a hidden website described elsewhere in this review passes the suite. Add `website_name` here; the test should fail until the serializer guards that attribute.

findings.title: The equal-length subdomain branch of website_name is never exercised
findings.body: The three new examples cover `website_host == discourse_host`, the `else` branch, and the parent-domain case. None exercises the `elsif` branch (`website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length && ... > 2`), i.e. the `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` case named in the code comment, which is the most complex branch. The nil/invalid-website case (host cannot be parsed) is also untested.

findings.title: Subdomain comparison treats unrelated domains under multi-label public suffixes as equal
findings.body: The equivalence check removes only the first label of each host and compares the rest. For hosts whose public suffix has more than one label this is wrong: with website `http://foo.co.uk/post` and instance `bar.co.uk`, comparing `['foo','co','uk'][1..-1].join` with `['bar','co','uk'][1..-1].join` yields `co.uk` for both, so it reports the domains as the same and shows the full path `foo.co.uk/post`, even though `foo.co.uk` and `bar.co.uk` are unrelated registrable domains. Use a real registrable-domain/public-suffix comparison, or only treat the website as a subdomain of the instance when it actually ends with `.` + instance host (and vice versa).
